name: Endocrine Cascade Volatilization Lance ECVL-5 'Burnout'
description:
The ECVL-5 delivers a focused beam of targeted microwave-band radiation tuned to the resonant absorption frequencies of adrenal and thyroid tissue. On contact, the beam causes explosive volatilization of the target's endocrine glands — not through burning, but through a rapid-phase transition of the glandular fluid content that causes the tissue to rupture from internal pressure. The immediate effect is a catastrophic hormonal surge as the contents of the destroyed glands flood the bloodstream simultaneously: a single discharge produces cortisol, adrenaline, and thyroid hormone levels exceeding any naturally achievable state by orders of magnitude. The target does not simply collapse — they first experience approximately 8–14 seconds of extraordinary physiological activation before the system crashes.

Those 8–14 seconds are the weapon's defining characteristic and the source of its street name. Targets in the surge phase demonstrate superhuman short-term strength and pain tolerance, complete disregard for self-preservation, and in some cases auditory and visual hallucinations driven by the hormonal cascade. Operators who have not been briefed on this effect have been killed by targets they believed were already incapacitated. After the surge, the target collapses into complete endocrine failure — without immediate and aggressive medical intervention, death follows within 30–90 minutes. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS developed the resonance calibration data during research into targeted glandular therapy; the weaponized application was not their intent, but the data was stolen and sold to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS within eighteen months of the research being completed.

The weapon is long-form, resembling a conventional anti-materiel rifle, with a distinctive annular emitter ring at the muzzle. It requires precise targeting — the beam must contact the torso in the correct anatomical corridor to hit the adrenal glands — and comes equipped with a thermal imaging scope that highlights endocrine tissue through clothing and light cover. The weapon is considered one of the most ethically contested in GLMZ's black market, even among operators with few ethical constraints.
legality: Prohibited — classified as a method of torture and induced death
specifications:
effective range: 15–200 meters
targeting requirement: Torso hit within 8 cm of adrenal anatomical corridor
surge phase duration: 8–14 seconds post-strike
time to endocrine failure: Immediate post-surge
time to death without treatment: 30–90 minutes
power source: High-density microwave induction cell, 9 discharges
weight: 7.4 kg
length: 118 cm
scope: Thermal endocrine contrast imaging, 4x–16x magnification
known countermeasures: Microwave-reflective body armor (partial), endocrine shielding vest (experimental)
tactical_use: Used almost exclusively as an assassination tool where the operator wants to ensure death without a clean kill shot — the surge phase provides plausible cover ('the target attacked first') before the crash. In military applications it has been deployed to destroy a target's capability to function in a leadership role even if they survive: endocrine failure at this severity leaves survivors with permanent glandular dysfunction requiring lifelong pharmaceutical management. Some operators use the surge phase deliberately, deploying the weapon against a target in a crowd to cause the surging target to create chaos before collapsing.
cultural_context: The Burnout is known but rarely seen in GLMZ's street ecosystem — its limited circulation and extreme cost keep it out of ordinary criminal use. It is associated almost entirely with high-level corporate assassination and military black operations. The phrase 'burning someone out' has taken on a secondary meaning in executive circles, referring to any operation that destroys a person's long-term functional capacity while leaving them technically alive. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS has quietly funded multiple legal challenges to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS over the stolen research data, but the cases have been repeatedly suppressed. Among street medics, a Burnout victim is considered one of the most difficult emergency presentations possible.

story_hooks: A LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS researcher is found dead of apparent endocrine failure — but the company's own weapon-attribution team confirms a Burnout discharge. Someone is using the weapon against the very company whose data created it. Why?

A character witnesses a Burnout strike in a public market — the target surges, kills two bystanders, then crashes. The operator vanished. The party must find the shooter before the target's death is ruled a spontaneous medical event.

An underground endocrinologist claims to have developed a pharmaceutical protocol that can prevent Burnout death if administered within the surge window — but the treatment is itself highly illegal and the knowledge makes her a target.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS approaches the party to recover a stolen ECVL-5 before it can be reverse-engineered by a competitor. The weapon is somewhere in the lower tiers. So is the person who stole it — and they're still alive, which means they haven't been found yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, menacing long-form rifle with an unnervingly organic aesthetic — the barrel tapers toward a distinctive ring-shaped emitter at the muzzle that resembles a predatory iris. The overall silhouette is predatory and clinical simultaneously, with an almost skeletal frame emphasizing the precision instrument beneath the surface.
physical_description.dimensions: 118 cm length overall, 28 cm width at scope mount, 12 cm height at receiver. Barrel section 76 cm. Annular emitter ring diameter 4.2 cm with 0.8 cm wall thickness.
physical_description.weight_description: 7.4 kg — substantial and deliberate, with weight distributed forward toward the emitter. Balanced on the scope mount, settling with purposeful heaviness in the shoulder. Not unwieldy, but demands respect and control.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber reinforced polymer chassis with anodized aluminum receiver and scope rail. The annular emitter is precision-cast tungsten-alloy with embedded microwave waveguide matrix.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray polymer with brushed aluminum accents. The emitter ring displays a distinctive oil-slick iridescence — nanometric coating that helps dissipate thermal bleed. Micro-abrasion marks suggest field use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominants: gunmetal gray and charcoal black. Accents: anodized silver-blue on the scope rail and power cell housing. The emitter ring gleams with dark rainbow sheen.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with embedded cooling channels (warm to touch after discharge). Forward grip is wrapped in thin heat-resistant synthetic cord for precision handling.
distinctive_features: Annular emitter ring at muzzle with visible waveguide segmentation
Thermal endocrine contrast scope mounted on raised rail — 4x-16x magnification with amber reticle
Power cell housing on right side: hexagonal medical-grade battery indicator with three LED status lights (green/amber/red)
Precision anatomical measurement marks etched into the scope's windage adjustment — numbered torso corridor reference points
Heat dissipation fins running along the barrel in a wave pattern
Microwave shielding panels with subtle ribbing along the receiver sides
Serial plate stamped with ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo and a blocky alphanumeric ID code
Discharge counter dial on the left side of the power cell housing (mechanical, not digital — 9 slots, movable indicator)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (stylized command triangle with downward arrow) stamped on the power cell housing and receiver. Serial number and date code on the left-side panel. Small warning triangle with microwave symbol repeated near the emitter ring and scope mount.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained but not pristine. Minor scuffs on the polymer chassis, slight discoloration around the emitter from thermal stress and residual phase-transition particulates. Scope lens shows faint dust shadows. Grip areas show wear from gloved handling. Battery indicator shows amber — unit is combat-ready but approaching mid-cycle on its power charge.
